faqs.a: The minimum is 3.5% if your credit score is 580 or higher. Scores between 500 and 579 require 10% down. These are national FHA rules; individual lenders may ask for more.
faqs.q: What is the minimum down payment for an FHA loan?

faqs.a: MIP (Mortgage Insurance Premium) is the FHA's version of private mortgage insurance. FHA charges two parts: an upfront MIP of 1.75% of the loan (usually rolled into the balance) and an annual MIP, about 0.55% per year for most 30-year loans, split into monthly payments.

Yes - in fact that is the norm. The 1.75% upfront MIP is almost always rolled into the loan balance, which is why this calculator adds it to the amount you borrow instead of asking you to pay it in cash.
faqs.q: Is the upfront MIP paid in cash?

faqs.a: It depends on your down payment. Put down less than 10% and MIP stays for the life of the loan. Put down 10% or more and MIP is removed after 11 years. You can also refinance into a conventional loan later to drop it.

Yes, FHA sets county loan limits that vary by area and change yearly. If the home price is above your county's limit, the loan cannot be an FHA loan. Check the current FHA limits for your county before house hunting.

The two MIP charges. A conventional loan with 20% down has no mortgage insurance at all, so its monthly payment is lower for the same home. FHA wins when your savings or credit score cannot support a conventional loan - it is a trade-off, not a discount.
faqs.q: Why is FHA sometimes more expensive than conventional?

fha-loan-calculator.formula:
Base loan = home price - down payment
Upfront MIP = 1.75% x base loan (added to the balance)
Monthly P&I = total loan x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n), with r = annual rate/12, n = years x 12
Monthly MIP = 0.55% x total loan / 12
Total monthly payment = P&I + MIP
howTo: Enter the home price you are considering.
Set your down payment percent - 3.5% is the FHA minimum with a credit score of 580 or higher.
Enter the quoted interest rate and the loan term in years.
Read the breakdown: principal and interest, monthly MIP, and the total monthly payment.
Compare scenarios by changing the down payment or rate before you talk to a lender.
keyFacts: FHA loans are insured by the Federal Housing Administration and allow down payments as low as 3.5%.
Upfront MIP is 1.75% of the base loan and is usually rolled into the loan balance.
Annual MIP (about 0.55% for most 30-year loans) is split into 12 monthly payments.
With less than 10% down, MIP stays for the life of the loan; with 10% or more it drops off after 11 years.
FHA loans have county loan limits and require the home to be your primary residence.
